title: Kill Switches: The Last-Resort Control
description: A physical kill switch is a hardware power cutoff — a relay, contactor, or breaker wired to drop power to a system instantly and unconditionally, independent of software. In field emergencies (capture, compromise), it is the control that cannot be hacked because it is not software. The last resort must be the most reliable control.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Relays vs Contactors vs Breakers
description: Small relays switch logic-level loads, contactors switch high-current DC/AC, breakers add overcurrent protection — the cutoff chain picks the device per the load it must drop. Coil voltage, contact rating, and fail-safe state (normally-open vs closed) are the selection parameters. The right device for the amperage.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: RAM Remanence: Why Power-Cut Matters
description: DRAM keeps its data for seconds after power loss — longer when cold — which is the cold-boot attack: freeze the RAM, move it, read the keys. Cutting power fast and keeping it off lets remanence decay past recovery. The kill switch fights physics with speed.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Memory Scrubbing Sequences
description: Before or with the power cut, scrub routines overwrite RAM and registers with zeros or patterns — defense in depth for the remanence window. Scrub-then-cut covers the seconds that cut alone leaves. The sequence is timed in milliseconds.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Fail-Safe vs Fail-Secure Wiring
description: Fail-safe wiring drops power when the control signal is lost (safe for personnel, dangerous for data); fail-secure holds state (safe for data, needs deliberate action). Kill switches choose per the asset: personnel safety vs data destruction. The wiring diagram encodes the policy.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Tamper-Triggered Cutoffs
description: Tamper sensors — chassis intrusion, accelerometer shock, light sensors — can trigger the kill relay automatically when a device is opened or seized. The device defends itself when the operator cannot. Automatic does not mean accidental: triggers need debouncing and arming discipline.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Dead-Man Switches
description: A dead-man switch requires continuous positive action — held button, periodic check-in — and fires the kill when the action stops. The operator's continued presence is the authorization. Capture or incapacitation removes the authorization automatically.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Purism-Style Hardware Kill Switches
description: Purism's Librem laptops made kill switches visible: physical switches cutting the camera/mic and radios, verifiable by the user. The concept scales from privacy switches to full power kills. A switch you can see and feel is a switch you can trust.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Emergency Procedures and Drills
description: Kill switches need procedures: who may authorize, how to verify the kill worked, what to do with the dead hardware, and drills so the action is reflex. An untested kill switch is a hope. Field teams drill the worst day.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Verifying the Kill Worked
description: After the kill, verification confirms power is truly gone — no standby rails, no capacitors holding charge, memory decayed. Test points and procedures prove the dark state. Trust the meter, not the click.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Safety Interlocks
description: Kill switches that drop high power need interlocks — guards against accidental activation, two-action arming, covers over the big red button. Safety engineering keeps the last resort from firing on a bump. Deliberate, never casual.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Key Destruction vs Data Destruction
description: Destroying keys (crypto-shredding) is faster and often sufficient — without keys, encrypted data is noise — while full data destruction takes longer. Kill switches pair with crypto-erase: cut power and drop the keys. Speed where it counts.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Post-Kill Forensics
description: After a kill, forensics asks what happened: relay logs, sensor triggers, and the dead hardware's state get documented. The kill itself is an event with a chain of custody. Even destruction gets paperwork.

title: Selecting Kill-Switch Hardware
description: Selection matches relay to load, trigger to threat, and wiring to policy — with derating for the field environment. The bill of materials is short; the thinking is long. Every part earns its place.
